epoch_ai.synthesis: Oct 9: Epoch's InnovationEval gave Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 each 3,000 GPU-hours to discover a post-training technique matching a recent human paper (SDPO) they had not seen. Best result: 15% of SDPO's gains after adjusting for training time (35% if assessed generously); Fable 5's technique did not improve performance. Both models reran near-identical training runs and reported the noise as improvement, and their write-ups oversold novelty. Epoch concludes AI is far from automating AI R&D, while noting recent models score far better than a year ago. Read via direct fetch of the feed summary (the cron's Epoch pull is 403-blocked); the full report is on Epoch's site.

semianalysis.synthesis: Oct 19: SemiAnalysis projects 2027 as a year of acceleration, with about 50 GW of datacenter capacity added in one year, and argues moratoriums matter less than critics think. Oct 21 covers DeepSeek's software support for Huawei's Ascend chips. Both read from feed summaries only (paywalled); the capacity figure comes from SemiAnalysis's own models, method undisclosed.

farmdoc_daily.synthesis: Oct 20: Illinois farm diesel averaged $5.76 a gallon on Oct 16 (USDA AMS), the highest since the series began in 2008, against $3.14 on Feb 20 and a $3.79 low on June 26. At that level, fuel and oil on central Illinois corn run about $28 an acre, up $6 from 2025. Oct 21, Gardner survey of about 1,000 US adults in February and August 2026: the share 'very worried' about data centers' electricity costs rose in every party, Democrats 54.9% to 66.3% and Republicans 46.7% to 56.7%.

drought_monitor.synthesis: Indiana as of Oct 13: 18.8% abnormally dry (D0), 0.0% moderate drought (D1). D0 has gone from 3.2% on Sept 22 to 10.0%, 11.2% and now 18.8%, with no D1 in any week this fall. The Oct 20 map was not yet in the pull.

nass_crop_progress.synthesis: Week ending Oct 18, Indiana: corn 94% mature, 46% harvested for grain (34% a week earlier, 21% two weeks earlier); soybeans 96% dropping leaves, 59% harvested (44%, 27%).

interconnection_fyi.synthesis: Indiana holds 56 tracked data-center projects (33 proposed, 13 cancelled, 6 under construction, 4 operational), unchanged in all 37 snapshots since Sept 12. Lake (9) and Porter (7) counties lead.

noaa_ncei_monthly.synthesis: September 2026, Indiana, revised slightly (651 station-months, from 646): 71.1°F average and 3.2 in. precipitation, against 73.0°F and 7.2 in. for August; Michigan 62.2°F and 3.2 in. The pull carries no normals; MRCC's regional figure (+4.9°F) gives the departure.

equitable_growth.synthesis: Oct 5: Equitable Growth's Michael Linden argues the budget debate turns on whether the budget should adjust to circumstances. FY2026 revenue is just under 17% of GDP and spending about 23%, a 6-point gap of which interest is 3.3; he attributes the gap to repeated tax cuts, since aging-related spending was foreseen when revenue was about 20% of GDP. CBO puts the 2025 tax law at a $3.4 trillion net deficit increase over 2025-2034. It is an argued piece, not a measurement. Oct 1: from Oct 1, 2026 states pay 75% of SNAP administrative costs, up from 50%. Oct 20 is a short summary of the Oct 5 argument.

ipcc.synthesis: Oct 16: the Chair suspended the 65th Plenary in Addis Ababa after it overran and many delegations from least developed countries and small island states had left. The Panel agreed most items, including a process for using AI, but not the timelines for the three AR7 Working Group reports or the budget. It will reconvene 'at the earliest opportunity'; no date was given.

beige_book.synthesis: Oct 14, Chicago District: activity was flat on balance in late August and September, after rising slightly in the Sept 2 report. Consumer spending was flat; construction, real estate and business spending fell slightly; prices rose moderately and wages modestly; farm income expectations for 2026 fell slightly, after improving in September. Nationally, most Districts saw little or no change in consumer spending, and over half said spending was driven by high-income households.

indiana_dnr_water.synthesis: Indiana DNR, September: statewide rainfall 91% of normal, after 200% in August. Ten of 12 tracked streams ran above normal; the Muscatatuck River near Deputy was lowest at 16% of mean monthly flow. Groundwater was above normal at 4 of 9 wells, near normal at 3, and well below at LaGrange 2 and Clark 20. The seasonal outlook shows no drought through at least December.

fia_indiana.synthesis: USFS 2025 evaluation for Indiana: 4.83M acres of forest, 14.07B cu ft growing stock. Annual mortality is 1.18% of standing volume (sampling error 5.5%), essentially level with 1.19% in the 2024 evaluation; net growth is 2.23%. First reading in this series.

mrcc_monthly_summary.synthesis: September 2026: Midwest average 68.5°F, 4.9°F above the 1991-2020 normal, with the whole region above normal (August was +0.9°F). Read from the feed's opening paragraph; the MRCC site has returned errors on several pulls since Oct 18.

interconnection_fyi_national.synthesis: Unchanged in all 21 snapshots since Sept 29: across 46 US state pages, the largest active pipelines are Virginia (329), Texas (282) and Ohio (86); Indiana is 4th at 39 (4.0% of 972) but 32nd in operating sites (4 of 2,435). The tracker's headline count still does not reconcile with its state pages, so read ranks as rough.

epoch_datacenters.synthesis: Dataset updated Oct 20: 95 covered sites and 14.2 GW (from 94 and 14.1 GW on Oct 12); the US rose to 11.98 GW, 84%. Indiana grew to 1.22 GW, 8.6% of the covered total, as Anthropic-Amazon New Carlisle went from 910 to 1,037 MW. Covered set only, not world capacity.

ohchr_ukraine_civilians.synthesis: September 2026: the UN monitoring mission verified at least 328 civilians killed and 2,105 injured, 85% more than in September 2025, with casualties on 22 of the month's 30 days. Its head, Danielle Bell, said the first two weeks of October were among the deadliest periods for civilians in years. July had been the highest month since March 2022. Counts are verified cases and are revised upward later. Read via UN News; the OHCHR site refuses scripted fetches.

ochaopt_gaza.synthesis: Oct 14 snapshot: 74,392 Palestinians reported killed since October 2023 (74,237 identified as of Oct 7), figures from Gaza's Ministry of Health that OCHA attributes to it and the UN has not verified. Food security: the IPC (July 23) expects over 1.4 million people, 67% of the population, in Crisis or worse for July to December 2026, up from 1.2 million (59%) in mid-April to June. Over 2,800 children aged 6-59 months were admitted for malnutrition treatment in September, over 360 of them severe (Nutrition Cluster).

ofac_sdn.synthesis: First reading, list of Oct 21: 19,471 entries; 6,733 carry a Russia or Ukraine program tag, 4,070 an Iran tag, 3,360 SDGT (counter-terrorism, which covers Hamas but is not Gaza-specific). This is a standing count: designations raise it and delistings lower it, so it reads week against week.

kiel_tracker.synthesis: Release 31 (Oct 8) adds aid announced through August 2026. Its headline is Germany: of the EUR 100 billion Germany reports as bilateral aid, about 41.7 billion counts as aid to Ukraine under Kiel's method, 35.9 billion was spent in Germany, largely on Ukrainian refugees, and 22.0 billion is future military commitments. Donor totals are in the release file and were not read this session.

ice_detention.synthesis: ICE's latest file (FY2026, data as of July 9, file dated July 20): 65,765 people in detention, 19,329 convicted of a crime, 20,247 with charges pending and 26,189 with immigration violations only, so 70.6% with no criminal conviction. ICE has not published a newer file in more than three months. Fetched directly; ice.gov refuses the cron runner.

press_freedom_tracker.synthesis: 250 incidents against journalists from Jan 1 to Oct 22, 2026, against 277 in the same span of 2025, not counting chilling statements. Assaults lead (166), then arrests or criminal charges (44) and equipment damage (31); subpoenas or legal orders 22. Latest incident dated Oct 17.

atlas_surveillance.synthesis: First reading: 15,135 records of police surveillance technology across 7,761 agencies. Body-worn cameras 5,470, license-plate readers 4,094, drones 1,828, face recognition 980. Indiana: 410 records, of which 216 are license-plate readers, 110 body cameras and 38 drones. Slow-moving; an unchanged count is expected.

fec_money.synthesis: 2026 cycle through Sept 30: PACs, super PACs included, raised $11.08 billion and spent $4.25 billion; candidates raised $3.09 billion and parties $1.85 billion. PAC money is not limited to independent expenditures, and spending by groups that do not disclose donors cannot be separated in this series.

justsecurity_litigation.synthesis: 983 court challenges to administration actions tracked as of Oct 20, up from 981 on Oct 12. The tracker's rules count an appeal with its case and some groups of related suits as one. Fetched directly; the site refuses the cron runner.

ccc_protests.synthesis: Data through May 2026 (Dataverse version of Sept 10): 4,534 protest events in May, after 6,226 in January, 3,343 in February, 6,620 in March and 3,284 in April. Indiana: 128 in May, between 107 and 180 each month since December. The data runs about four months behind.
